Below is an example of a complete `.gv` file that I created on a coffee shop's daily customer traffic.  Your final systems maps will looks something like this.   Use this example to follow along as you read through [DOT Explainer](DOT-Explainer.qmd)

This file is not posted on Canvas. Download it from the class GitHub page instead: [Coffee-Shop-Example-Graphviz.gv](https://github.com/profsmith-classes/pubh-402/blob/13f9f09f73e88d46ef9bc9b16a32d395e5de2c84/Coffee-Shop-Example-Graphviz.gv). Click the download button to download the file from the browser.

```
digraph CoffeeShopSystem {

  rankdir=TD;

  node [shape=box, style="rounded, filled", fillcolor="white", fontname="Arial"];

  edge [fontname="Arial", fontsize=10];

  // Team Number

  // Class Section

  // Team Member Names:

  // --- Nodes (5 elements) ---

  customers  [label="Daily customer count"];

  buzz       [label="Word-of-mouth / online buzz"];

  quality    [label="Coffee and service quality"];

  wait_time  [label="Average wait time in line"];

  staff      [label="Baristas scheduled per shift"];

  // --- Causal links (with polarity) ---

  customers -> buzz     [label="+"];         // More customers visiting generates more word-of-mouth and online reviews.

  buzz -> customers     [label="+ delay"];    // Positive buzz attracts new customers, though it takes time to spread and for people to act on it.

  quality -> buzz       [label="+"];         // Consistently good coffee and service generates positive buzz on its own, independent of how many people are currently visiting.

  customers -> wait_time [label="+"];        // More customers in the shop at once means longer lines.

  staff -> wait_time    [label="-"];         // More baristas working a shift serve customers faster, shortening the line.

  wait_time -> staff    [label="+ delay"];    // When wait times run long, the manager schedules more baristas for future shifts to compensate.

  // --- Loop callouts (subgraph clusters) ---

  subgraph cluster_R1 {

    label="R1 Reinforcing: word-of-mouth growth";
    style="rounded,dashed";
    color="gray40";
    fontname="Arial";
    fontsize=12;

    customers;
    buzz;

    /* More customers generate more buzz; more buzz attracts more customers. Both links are positive, so the effect compounds - the simplest possible reinforcing structure. */

  }

  subgraph cluster_B1 {

    label="B1 Balancing: staffing responds to wait times";
    style="rounded,dashed";
    color="gray40";
    fontname="Arial";
    fontsize=12;

    wait_time;
    staff;

    /* Long wait times prompt the manager to schedule more staff; more staff shortens the wait. One link positive, one negative - the loop corrects itself instead of compounding. */

  }

}
```
